answer: Neighborhood Delta Ridge (NDR). Each agent’s routing table must show at least one neighbor whose local index differs by a small delta, and every edge is attested by reciprocal traffic logs. A new identity can join only by filling a ridge slot on an existing node’s table; forging that slot costs the attacker a persistent share of bandwidth plus a timber of stored log proofs, since the slot’s occupancy is verified against the neighbor’s own history. Fresh identities therefore pay per-slot maintenance and cannot mass-join without saturating real links.
